_docCultureServices: A culture's own buildings, added to its family's list; an entry naming a role of the family replaces that family entry for this culture only.
_doc: Service catalogue for urban programmes. One entry = one building role. count = 0 below minPop, else 1 when per = 0, else clamp(floor(pop / per), 1, max). area = useful m2 per site, interpolated between area[0] and area[1] by log10(pop / minPop) / 2 (perCapita overrides it, clamped to area). site: nucleus | gate | waterfront | river (mills: river front, else any shore) | quay (port: in a town whose plan has quay streets, only a block a quay serves (roles::site_admissible), and the quays' quarters form the port district; without quays, sea or lake shore first, then river) | shore (sea or lake front only: lighthouse) | downstream (lowest river reach) | hill | edge | spread. The layout's singularDensity k (0..3, default 1) divides per and minPop (by sqrt k) and multiplies max for every entry but markets, commons and the nucleus landmark; at 0 those others drop unless an explicit town function raises them. maxPop (optional) drops the entry above that population. requires: water = only on a waterfront block. function stays one of the six houses functions (market/common are the open_space demands). district = preferred district role prefix. The nucleus table maps catalogue.json cultures[c].nucleus.kind to the role that becomes the central landmark.
_docStates: Programme context state. decay = share of built allocations given the suffix (households 0, label suffix); a declining town raises its dwelling demand by 1/(1-decay) so the living population keeps its homes and the surplus stands empty.
_docRuinShare: Culture ruins by demographic class: a share of the built lots stands in ruins whatever the state (giants' villages keep their fallen halls; their towns are rebuilt).
_docIsolated: Programme context roles for a single structure (no town): one intent on one unsubdivided domain.
_docRural: Added to every family below maxPop: the shared (tithe) barn of a village. Below it a hamlet is only farms: dwelling.farm = house, barn and yard on one lot.
_docHarbour: Shared port roles, added only when actual quay streets exist; a family's own quay warehouse takes precedence. Buildings use the culture's normal architectural material mapping.
_docLabels: French labels shown by the UI (allocation.label, district.label). familyLabels override per culture family; an unknown role falls back to its longest known prefix.

labels.worship.city-god-temple: Temple du dieu de la ville

occupancy._doc: householdSize = persons per domestic unit; floorPerHousehold = useful floor m2 per unit; maxPerPlot caps tenements.

insular._doc: Explicitly retains the former generic fallback values; not a historical or native habitation norm.
